title: Bakery profit
question: A bakery sells muffins for 35 rupees and cookies for 18 rupees. On Monday it sold 24 muffins and 40 cookies. On Tuesday it sold a quarter more muffins than on Monday, but 10 fewer cookies. It spends 40% of its two-day sales on ingredients. How much profit does it make over the two days?

title: Who owns the fish?
blurb: A five-house logic puzzle with exactly one solution (checked by computer).
question: Five people (Asha, Bilal, Chen, Dev and Esha) live in five houses in a row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Each owns a different pet: a cat, a dog, a fish, a bird or a rabbit. Clues: 1) Chen lives in house 1. 2) Dev lives in the house immediately to the right of Esha. 3) The bird owner lives in house 5. 4) Bilal owns the dog. 5) Asha lives next to the cat owner. 6) Esha does not own the fish. 7) The rabbit owner lives immediately to the left of the dog owner. 8) Chen does not own the cat. Who owns the fish?

title: Who finished third?
blurb: A race-order puzzle with exactly one solution (checked by computer).
question: Five runners (Ana, Bo, Cy, Di and Ed) finish a race with no ties. Clues: 1) Ana finished before Bo. 2) Cy finished immediately after Di. 3) Ed did not finish first or last. 4) Bo finished after Cy. 5) Ana finished before Di. 6) Ed finished before Cy. Who finished third?

title: Who took the cake?
blurb: A who-is-telling-the-truth puzzle with exactly one solution (checked by computer).
question: One of four people took the cake: Mia, Noah, Omar or Pia. Exactly one of the four statements below is true, and the other three are false. Mia says: "Noah took it." Noah says: "Omar took it." Omar says: "Noah is lying." Pia says: "I did not take it." Who took the cake?

title: Merge time slots
blurb: Write a small Python function. We run it against test cases to see if it works.
question: Write a Python function merge_slots(slots) that takes a list of [start, end] pairs (whole numbers, start <= end, in any order) and returns a list of merged pairs sorted by start. Slots that overlap or touch (for example [1, 3] and [3, 5]) must be merged into one. Example: merge_slots([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10], [9, 12]]) returns [[1, 6], [8, 12]]. An empty list returns an empty list.

title: Balanced brackets
blurb: Write a small Python function. We run it against test cases to see if it works.
question: Write a Python function is_balanced(text) that returns True if every bracket in the text is closed in the right order, and False otherwise. The brackets are (), [] and {}. All other characters are ignored. Example: is_balanced('{[()]}') returns True and is_balanced('(]') returns False. An empty string returns True.

title: Roman numerals

question: Write a Python function roman_to_int(text) that converts a Roman numeral (capital letters I, V, X, L, C, D, M) to a whole number. A smaller symbol placed before a larger one is subtracted, for example IV is 4 and IX is 9. Example: roman_to_int('MCMXCIV') returns 1994.

title: Flatten a nested list

question: Write a Python function flatten(items) that takes a list which may contain other lists nested to any depth, and returns one flat list with the same values in the same order. Example: flatten([1, [2, [3, 4]], 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. An empty list returns an empty list.
